opportunities.title: registerUser access token can reference a different user id
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `registerUser()` currently builds the returned `id` and the JWT `sub` with two separate `Date.now()` calls. If time advances between those calls, the API can return one user id while signing an access token for a different subject. Downstream authenticated requests would then identify a different user than the one returned by registration. ## Expected fix Generate the new user id once, return that id, and sign the access token with the same id as `sub`. Add a regression test that forces the timestamp to advance between calls and verifies the token subject matches the returned id. ## Scope This issue is limited to the registration response/token subject mismatch in `apps/api/src/services/authService.js` plus focused API service test coverage. This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information. References #743.

opportunities.title: [Bounty: $100] Admin dispatch/refund re-hash the event-derived order id so they can never match the on-chain order
opportunities.summary: **Context** dispatchOrder and refundOrder in lib/stellar/orders.ts run await hashOrderId(orderId) (lines 222, 303) before invoking the contract, i.e. they expect the raw pre-image ("SS-..."). But app/admin/orders/page.tsx builds its order rows exclusively from indexer events whose order_id topic is the already-hashed 32-byte value, and passes that hex to onDispatch/onRefund (page.tsx:140,154). SHA-256 is one-way, so hashing the hex again can never reproduce the stored BytesN<32> and dispatch/refund fail with OrderNotFound. **Proposed Change** Make dispatchOrder/refundOrder accept an already-hashed 64-hex order id without re-hashing it (only hash short raw ids), e.g. via a small resolveOrderIdHash helper with both paths unit-tested, and keep the admin page passing the event-derived id unchanged. **Acceptance Criteria** - Add a pure helper that returns raw bytes for a short pre-image and passes a 64-hex input through unchanged; unit-test both paths - Test asserts the admin page passes the event-derived hex id into dispatchOrder/refundOrder unmodified - npm run test and npm run type-check pass **Suggested Label**: bug **ETA:** 24 hours

opportunities.title: upload endpoint accepts empty file submissions as successful uploads
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `POST /api/uploads` currently returns `201` with `success: true` even when the multipart request does not include a `file` field. The response reports `status: "no-file"`, but it is still treated as a successful upload by HTTP status and response shape. ## Expected fix Reject upload requests that do not include a file with a clear `400` response, and keep successful upload responses reserved for requests that actually include `req.file`. Add route-level regression coverage for the missing-file case. ## Scope This issue is limited to missing-file handling in `POST /api/uploads` and focused API test coverage. This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
